localBiteReport: Water temperature is 76°F. The most current report this week (Oct 23–29, 2026) from Great Days Outdoors covers Choctawhatchee Bay directly: the redfish bite on the bay flats has held up well even in the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, with fish under about 23 inches still holding in familiar guts and potholes in the shallows. Larger upper-slot and overslot reds are transitioning into a more mobile fall pattern across the bay. A local charter guide noted that after a recent cold front, cut mullet chunks on Carolina rigs outperformed live bait for reds on the flats — a useful tactical note as water cools. A guide report posted about a week ago on Captain Experiences also flagged that redfish and trout are heating up in the bayous as the Destin Fishing Rodeo gets underway for October.
